item.title: Angel Reese hits 3-pointer vs. Valkyries in Game 7, but will history hold?
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Angel Reese hits 3-pointer vs. Valkyries in Game 7, but will history hold? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries are locked in a battle during Game 7 of the WNBA Finals for the right to host the WNBA trophy, and if statistics hold, history is on the side of the Dream. Angel Reese knocked down a 3-pointer in the first quarter of Game 7, and the Dream are 16-0 this year when she hits at least one 3-point shot, as per Annie Costabile of The Athletic. Angel Reese has incorporated the 3-pointer into her offensive arsenal this season, her first with the Dream. During the WNBA playoffs so far, she has taken a total of 23 attempts from the 3-point line coming into Game 7, while converting on 10 of them (38.5 percent). That’s a significant increase in efficiency from the regular season when Reese took 57 3-point attempts and knocked down 11 of them (19.3 percent). But during her first two seasons in the WNBA with the Chicago Sky, she took a combined 38 attempts from the 3-point line. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The No. 7 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft by the Sky, Reese was traded to the Dream before the start of the regular season. She was the league’s Defensive Player of the Year this season and was selected to her third consecutive All-Star appearance. Coming into Game 7, Reese had been averaging 16.8 points, 10.9 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.6 blocked shots with splits of 41.7 percent shooting from the field, 38.5 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 79.7 percent shooting from the free-throw line. This is her first career playoff appearance. As of publication, Reese had five points and seven rebounds in 17 minutes by halftime. Related: Dream’s Jordin Canada sets WNBA Finals career-high in scoring vs. Valkyries Related: Here’s what Geno Auriemma thinks about Dream-Valkyries WNBA Finals Game 7

item.title: LA Galaxy Sweep Aside Austin 4-1 at Home
item.description: LA Galaxy Winger Robert Taylor and Midfielder Marco Reus celebrate a goal during the Galaxy's 4-1 home win over Austin FC on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Dignity Health Sports Park. G's Earn Victory in Must-Win Home Match Los Angeles, Calif. -- As far as Fan Appreciation Nights go, it couldn’t have gone better for the LA Galaxy. Marco Reus led the way with a trio of assists, Hirving “Chucky” Lozano tallied a header in his return to the starting 11, and Sergi Roberto scored his first Galaxy goal in a 4-1 home demolition of visiting Austin FC on October 31, 2026. The controlled, if somewhat wasteful win was vital, as nothing short of three points would have put the Galaxy’s playoff destiny out of their own hands. W's in the chat ‼️ pic.twitter.com/72399LmOBm — LA Galaxy (@LAGalaxy) October 31, 2026 Instead, LA Galaxy Head Coach Greg Vanney’s team took care of business from the first whistle in a professional victory they absolutely dared not drop points in. More importantly, it showed LA can win the necessary matches on their fixture list if they are to make it to the postseason. “Yeah, it was good,” Vanney said of his team’s performance. The Galaxy boss had the benefit of starting all three DP’s for the first time today, and it showed. “You know, I think some of that comes from the group of players as well that we have. Right, there's quality on the field. They take care of some of those moments and some of the business.” “I think guys now are starting to fit into their roles and starting to connect together. And so, you know, I could say today we didn't have a great day today, but we still were able to win four-one. And so that's good. That means, you know, for us that when we have a great day, we can be really, really good.” Starting Brightly The Galaxy set the tone early. An errant Ilie Sánchez pass was picked off by Harbor Miller, who advanced on the right channel and found João Klauss in the middle of the box. The Galaxy DP used soft feet to control the ball and pass into the bottom right of the net. The goal, Klauss’ 10th of the season, put the Galaxy up 1-0 inside 10 minutes. LA pressures and creates the turnover. 💪 Joao Klauss with the finish to put them ahead. 💥 📺 Apple TV: https://t.co/zbc3az1hE8 pic.twitter.com/wR2CtTqhvV — Major League Soccer (@MLS) October 31, 2026 Austin Goalkeeper Damian Las made several saves to keep the Galaxy at bay, but try as Las might, he could not stem the tide indefinitely. Reus made sure of it. After a botched Verde clearance in the 38th minute, Miller found Reus on the right wing, and the former German international sent a clipped pass into the area. Incredibly, the diminutive Lozano out-jumped the entire Austin defense and headed it home to give the Galaxy a 2-0 lead. The goal marked Lozano's first home goal of the season. item.content:encoded: LA Galaxy Winger Robert Taylor and Midfielder Marco Reus celebrate a goal during the Galaxy's 4-1 home win over Austin FC on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Dignity Health Sports Park. G's Earn Victory in Must-Win Home Match Los Angeles, Calif. -- As far as Fan Appreciation Nights go, it couldn’t have gone better for the LA Galaxy. Marco Reus led the way with a trio of assists, Hirving “Chucky” Lozano tallied a header in his return to the starting 11, and Sergi Roberto scored his first Galaxy goal in a 4-1 home demolition of visiting Austin FC on October 31, 2026. The controlled, if somewhat wasteful win was vital, as nothing short of three points would have put the Galaxy’s playoff destiny out of their own hands. W's in the chat ‼️ pic.twitter.com/72399LmOBm — LA Galaxy (@LAGalaxy) October 31, 2026 Instead, LA Galaxy Head Coach Greg Vanney’s team took care of business from the first whistle in a professional victory they absolutely dared not drop points in. More importantly, it showed LA can win the necessary matches on their fixture list if they are to make it to the postseason. “Yeah, it was good,” Vanney said of his team’s performance. The Galaxy boss had the benefit of starting all three DP’s for the first time today, and it showed. “You know, I think some of that comes from the group of players as well that we have. Right, there's quality on the field. They take care of some of those moments and some of the business.” “I think guys now are starting to fit into their roles and starting to connect together. And so, you know, I could say today we didn't have a great day today, but we still were able to win four-one. And so that's good. That means, you know, for us that when we have a great day, we can be really, really good.” Starting Brightly The Galaxy set the tone early. An errant Ilie Sánchez pass was picked off by Harbor Miller, who advanced on the right channel and found João Klauss in the middle of the box. The Galaxy DP used soft feet to control the ball and pass into the bottom right of the net. The goal, Klauss’ 10th of the season, put the Galaxy up 1-0 inside 10 minutes. LA pressures and creates the turnover. 💪 Joao Klauss with the finish to put them ahead. 💥 📺 Apple TV: https://t.co/zbc3az1hE8 pic.twitter.com/wR2CtTqhvV — Major League Soccer (@MLS) October 31, 2026 Austin Goalkeeper Damian Las made several saves to keep the Galaxy at bay, but try as Las might, he could not stem the tide indefinitely. Reus made sure of it. After a botched Verde clearance in the 38th minute, Miller found Reus on the right wing, and the former German international sent a clipped pass into the area. Incredibly, the diminutive Lozano out-jumped the entire Austin defense and headed it home to give the Galaxy a 2-0 lead. The goal marked Lozano's first home goal of the season. For a returning Lozano, the goal was a welcome sight. But for the Galaxy, Chucky’s reintegration and return to the scoresheet could give them another threat as they try to put everything together before their final match and any potential playoff run. LA Galaxy Winger Hirving Miguel Mota LA Galaxy Winger Hirving "Chucky" Lozano scored in his return to the starting 11, in the Galaxy's 4-1 home win over Austin FC on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Dignity Health Sports Park. Although Lozano lasted just 45 minutes, his cameo was more than encouraging. “The truth is I’m very happy to have gotten the opportunity to play,” Lozano told the Sporting Tribune. “I was a little bit afraid because of the injury, but as the minutes went by, I gained more confidence and, well, thankfully, I was able to score, and the important thing is that we added three points that are very important.” Two Halves, Two Goals in Each Three minutes after the restart, Robert Taylor contributed to the rout. Reus found the substitute in the middle of the Austin box, who kept his composure to blast the ball into the roof of the net for the 3-0 score. Robert Taylor TOP BINS 🎯 pic.twitter.com/zDhiiRCU7H — LA Galaxy (@LAGalaxy) October 31, 2026 The afternoon's only notable blemish came six minutes later. The Galaxy defense gave Austin Midfielder Ervin Torres too much space, and the 18-year-old let loose with a 25-yard curling effort that LA Galaxy Goalkeeper JT Marcinkowski could only flail at to make it 3-1. But that's as close as Austin got on the day. The Galaxy took the goal on the chin and immediately set upon scoring another. And it would be Reus who would set the table once again. Klauss started the play, and his volleyed pass found Reus in stride. Reus headed the pass down to Roberto, who made no mistake in adding to the lead to make it 4-1 for the G’s. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Major League Soccer (@mls) The win temporarily puts the Galaxy seventh in the Western Conference table, with Sunday matches left to play. It means LA is unbeaten at home in eight matches and unbeaten in four games in all competitions. It was also exactly the kind of response Galaxy fans and the maker of the first goal, Miller, wanted to see. “You know, you see us dropping those points to some of the teams lower on the table earlier in the season, and I think now it's like, okay, hey, this is not acceptable,” Miller explained of the early-season setbacks. “We've learned from those, and I think it's been huge to get on top of games early for us. You know, we always end up having to come back or having to make the game much more difficult on ourselves. So I think in a night like tonight, we put away some chances early.” Taking Care of Business In a season where the Galaxy have been inconsistent and dropped points to teams much lower in the table, the professional victory was gratifying and a lift for an LA team that faces another must-win next week on Decision Day. LA Galaxy Striker João Klauss waves to the crowd after scoring the opening goal in the Galaxy's 4-1 home win over Austin FC on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Dignity Health Sports Park. Miguel Mota LA Galaxy Striker João Klauss waves to the crowd after scoring the opening goal in the Galaxy's 4-1 home win over Austin FC on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Dignity Health Sports Park. The Galaxy will need a repeat performance next week as they play for their playoff lives and try to extend their season away at Real Salt Lake. RSL is currently just two points back of the Galaxy, and a win will see them leapfrog them and potentially keep them out of the postseason. It is simple for LA, though. Win, and they’re in to the postseason. It also sends them into the playoffs in potentially their best form of the campaign. “I think we’ll be able to advance,” Lozano stated confidently when asked about Decision Day. “We have a great team. We hope everything comes out in our favor, and well, if we make it to the playoffs, I think it’ll be a different story.” The Galaxy and Real Salt Lake face off on Decision Day, next Saturday, November 7, at 4:00 p.m. for a postseason berth.

item.title: Oregon football rallies past Northwestern after chaotic week
item.description: It was a week of distractions for the Oregon football team in a season that’s been full of them. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after a lackluster loss to Illinois, another player was arrested , and it was announced that star quarterback Dante Moore won’t play again this season due to injury. The fanbase appeared to show its frustration by not filling Autzen Stadium – or the tailgate lots during pregame – on a cold but dry afternoon Oct. 31 for a game against No. 18 Northwestern. Official attendance was 55,673, but anyone with eyes could see the empty rows around the top of the stadium. The Ducks showed that while many are giving up on them, they’re not giving up on themselves, rallying from a two-touchdown deficit to beat the Wildcats, 34-26. Oregon (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten Conference), which trailed 20-6 in the second quarter and 20-13 at halftime, was led by beleaguered quarterback Dylan Raiola. Raiola threw for 336 yards and three touchdowns, including a pair to wide receiver Dakorien Moore, who had seven catches for 128 yards. “I mean, let me tell you this has been a crazy season,” said Raiola, who transferred from Nebraska in the offseason with the expectation of playing behind Dante Moore for a season. “The ups and downs, the in between. Like, I can’t say enough of how proud I am of this team. The way they just show up every day and keep attacking. … They just fight for each other. It’s pretty cool to see.” Raiola has been hot or cold – but rarely both – in the games he has played since Moore was injured against USC on Sept. 26. Saturday, he heated up as the game went on and found his groove in the second half. He actually looked really good on his final throw of the first half when he dropped a dime to Moore in the corner of the end zone for a 10-yard TD with 55 seconds left before halftime. Raiola was 12 for 17 in the second half for 214 yards, including a 17-yard touchdown throw to tight end Jamari Johnson that cut the Ducks ’ deficit to three points, 23-20, in the third quarter. With 10:20 to play in the game and Oregon leading 27-23, Raiola delivered the dagger with a 75-yard bomb to Dakorien Moore, who caught the ball at the Northwestern 33 and went untouched into the end zone. “I felt like the rhythm that we’ve been searching for showed up in big moments,” Oregon coach Dan Lanning said. “I thought our quarterback played with a lot of confidence and was able to execute.” Raiola’s last pass was also memorable as he casually flicked the ball over a pack of defenders to Johnson, who made a bobbling, 18-yard catch as he fell onto his backside on third-and-8. The play secured a first down and allowed the Ducks to kneel out the final 1:20 of the game. “He made a big play, but I don’t know if that was wide open,” Lanning said with a wry smile. “It played out a little differently than we thought it would, but players make plays. item.content:encoded: It was a week of distractions for the Oregon football team in a season that’s been full of them. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after a lackluster loss to Illinois, another player was arrested , and it was announced that star quarterback Dante Moore won’t play again this season due to injury. The fanbase appeared to show its frustration by not filling Autzen Stadium – or the tailgate lots during pregame – on a cold but dry afternoon Oct. 31 for a game against No. 18 Northwestern. Official attendance was 55,673, but anyone with eyes could see the empty rows around the top of the stadium. The Ducks showed that while many are giving up on them, they’re not giving up on themselves, rallying from a two-touchdown deficit to beat the Wildcats, 34-26. Oregon (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten Conference), which trailed 20-6 in the second quarter and 20-13 at halftime, was led by beleaguered quarterback Dylan Raiola. Raiola threw for 336 yards and three touchdowns, including a pair to wide receiver Dakorien Moore, who had seven catches for 128 yards. “I mean, let me tell you this has been a crazy season,” said Raiola, who transferred from Nebraska in the offseason with the expectation of playing behind Dante Moore for a season. “The ups and downs, the in between. Like, I can’t say enough of how proud I am of this team. The way they just show up every day and keep attacking. … They just fight for each other. It’s pretty cool to see.” Raiola has been hot or cold – but rarely both – in the games he has played since Moore was injured against USC on Sept. 26. Saturday, he heated up as the game went on and found his groove in the second half. He actually looked really good on his final throw of the first half when he dropped a dime to Moore in the corner of the end zone for a 10-yard TD with 55 seconds left before halftime. Raiola was 12 for 17 in the second half for 214 yards, including a 17-yard touchdown throw to tight end Jamari Johnson that cut the Ducks ’ deficit to three points, 23-20, in the third quarter. With 10:20 to play in the game and Oregon leading 27-23, Raiola delivered the dagger with a 75-yard bomb to Dakorien Moore, who caught the ball at the Northwestern 33 and went untouched into the end zone. “I felt like the rhythm that we’ve been searching for showed up in big moments,” Oregon coach Dan Lanning said. “I thought our quarterback played with a lot of confidence and was able to execute.” Raiola’s last pass was also memorable as he casually flicked the ball over a pack of defenders to Johnson, who made a bobbling, 18-yard catch as he fell onto his backside on third-and-8. The play secured a first down and allowed the Ducks to kneel out the final 1:20 of the game. “He made a big play, but I don’t know if that was wide open,” Lanning said with a wry smile. “It played out a little differently than we thought it would, but players make plays. We’ll coach the moment. He told me as soon as he came off the field, ‘I owe you one.’ I know that was a little bit careless, but don’t you love that a little bit as a coach?” There wasn't much not to like about how Raiola and the Ducks performed in the second half, giving Oregon and its fans a positive ending to week that started out anything but. “We weren’t going to go down without swinging,” Raiola said. “I think we kind of lost that a little bit. I don’t think we completely lost it, but we got back to our DNA and I’m proud of our guys.” Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men’s basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com . Want to see more Oregon Ducks coverage? Subscribe to The Register-Guard’s newsletter . item.title: Boston College Men’s Hockey Falls to Northeastern 4-3
item.description: The Boston College men’s hockey team dropped the second game of their weekend series with Northeastern on Saturday night, falling to their conference rivals by a 4-3 score. After taking Friday night’s game in overtime, the Eagles lost this one in the exact same fashion, as the Huskies found the game winning goal just two minutes into the extra frame. The Eagles jumped out to an early lead for the second night in a row, though now quite as quickly as they did on Friday night. After getting a few good chances in the opening shifts, BC got their first pwoer play chance of the night just over four minutes into the game and made it count almost immediately, when Dean Letourneau continued his red hot start to the season by ripping a shot from the slot into the back of the net for his fifth goal of the season. Pelletier sets up Dean for the early power play goal! 📺 NESN pic.twitter.com/KJVY0avmmS — BC Men's Hockey (@BC_MHockey) October 31, 2026 Unlike last night, however, Northeastern was able to push back a bit after falling behind, and Louka Cloutier had to be sharp in net for the remainder of the period to keep it a 1-0 game, as the Huskies had a number of high quality chances to tie things up, inclduing one late in the period when BC lost track of a Northeastern player right in front of the net. Big stop from Clouts towards the end of the first! 📺 NESN pic.twitter.com/iVasbghLU5 — BC Men's Hockey (@BC_MHockey) October 31, 2026 Cloutier was sharp early on in the second period as well, as Northeastern continued to apply pressure and look for a tying goal. item.content:encoded: The Boston College men’s hockey team dropped the second game of their weekend series with Northeastern on Saturday night, falling to their conference rivals by a 4-3 score. After taking Friday night’s game in overtime, the Eagles lost this one in the exact same fashion, as the Huskies found the game winning goal just two minutes into the extra frame. The Eagles jumped out to an early lead for the second night in a row, though now quite as quickly as they did on Friday night. After getting a few good chances in the opening shifts, BC got their first pwoer play chance of the night just over four minutes into the game and made it count almost immediately, when Dean Letourneau continued his red hot start to the season by ripping a shot from the slot into the back of the net for his fifth goal of the season. Pelletier sets up Dean for the early power play goal! 📺 NESN pic.twitter.com/KJVY0avmmS — BC Men's Hockey (@BC_MHockey) October 31, 2026 Unlike last night, however, Northeastern was able to push back a bit after falling behind, and Louka Cloutier had to be sharp in net for the remainder of the period to keep it a 1-0 game, as the Huskies had a number of high quality chances to tie things up, inclduing one late in the period when BC lost track of a Northeastern player right in front of the net. Big stop from Clouts towards the end of the first! 📺 NESN pic.twitter.com/iVasbghLU5 — BC Men's Hockey (@BC_MHockey) October 31, 2026 Cloutier was sharp early on in the second period as well, as Northeastern continued to apply pressure and look for a tying goal. They finally managed to break through with a power play tally, scoring on a one-timer just about nine minutes in to the second period. They took their first lead of the weekend a few minutes later with their second power play goal of the period to make it a 2-1 game. The Eagles were able to get things back on level terms with a power play goal with 3:21 left in the period, when Alex Pelletier managed to put home a rebound off of a shot from Luka Radivojevic for his first collegiate goal. THE REBOUND. What a first GOALLLLL for Pelletier! 📺 NESN pic.twitter.com/qd857CqzXu — BC Men's Hockey (@BC_MHockey) November 1, 2026 Jake Sondreal made it a 3-2 game with his first of the season barely more than a minute later, finishing a chance off of a rebound this time off of a shot from Pelletier to give BC the lead back heading into the third period. Coast to coast 😎 📺 NESN pic.twitter.com/qiL7rQZin4 — BC Men's Hockey (@BC_MHockey) November 1, 2026 Northeastern made it a 3-3 game with a goal just three minutes into the third period, jumping on a loose puck after Kristian Kostadinski blocked a shot in the slot. Both teams had their chances over the rest of the period, including a power play opportunity for BC with just over two minutes left in regulation, but the two goalies both made some timely saves and we went to overtime for the second night in a row. It was Northeastern who found the back of the net in the overtime period this time, scoring just over two minutes in on a rebound play after BC had a flurry of chances at the other end. The Eagles dropped a winnable game by a 4-3 score and failed to complete the weekend sweep. This game felt a lot like Friday night’s contest, with BC putting up a bunch of chances but not finishing on more than a few of them and letting Northeastern stick around for longer than they should have. It didn’t cost them anything on Friday night fortunately, but on Saturday, their lack of finishing bit them in the end. They’ll look to right the ship next week when they host Vermont for two more Hockey East games on Thursday and Friday night.

item.title: Alineaciones del América vs Toluca – Apertura 2026
item.description: Alineaciones del América vs Toluca – Apertura 2026 América estará enfrentando a Toluca en duelo de jornada 15 del Apertura 2026. Ambos equipos llegan a este partido con la necesidad de una victoria; las águilas necesitan tres puntos para mantener el liderato del torneo, mientras que Toluca busca afianzarse dentro de las primeras cuatro posiciones de la tabla. La alineación del América: Luis Malagón, Franco Rossano, Santiago Mingo, Santiago Bueno, Kevin Álvarez, Israel Reyes, Erick Sánchez, Carlos Álvarez, Isaías Violante, Brian Rodríguez y Henry Martín. En la banca estarán: Rodolfo Cota, Emilio Lara, Cristian Borja, Miguel Vázquez, Edwin Cerrillo, Alan Cervantes, Alexis Gutiérrez, Oscar Perea, Derek Jiménez y Miguel Borja. El 11 de Toluca: El partido dará inicio a las 09:10PM y será transmitido por Canal 5, TUDN, VIX Premium y Layvtime. Para Estados Unidos va por TUDN USA.

item.title: How SW Indiana teams, athletes fared at IHSAA cross country state finals
item.description: The IHSAA cross country state finals took place on October 31 in Terre Haute. Barr-Reeve and Reitz were the two boys teams that qualified from Southwestern Indiana. For the girls, it was Jasper. More: IHSAA cross country regionals recap for SW Indiana Several athletes from across Southwestern Indiana competed as well. Here’s how it went for the area. IHSAA boys cross country championships It was a good day for Jack Wilbourne of Signature School and Carter Zeiren of Reitz. two of Evansville’s best distance runners. Wilbourne finished in second place with a time of 15:00.4, still 26 seconds behind first place. Zeiren finished in sixth with a time of 15:09.5 Barr-Reeve finished 15th in team scoring, while Reitz finished 19th. Other individual results from Terre Haute: Paxton Traylor (Barr-Reeve, 16th, 15:24.3), Will Dierlam (Reitz, 17th, 15:24.4), Jaxon Seger (Northeast Dubois, 18th, 15:25.3), Lincoln Willoughby (North, 44th,15:45.7), Luke Underwood (Barr-Reeve, 70th, 16:00.1), Pierce Yoder (Barr-Reeve, 77th, 16:03.0), Austin Carlile (Castle, 85th, 16:07.0), Nate Hollinden (Tell City, 90th, 16:08.5), Graham Colvin (Barr-Reeve, 149th, 16:26.8), Caleb Hammonds (Reitz, 185th, 16:44.4), Landon Hartman (Memorial, 206th, 16:54.2), Robert Searcy (Reitz, 210th, 16:57.3), Noah Breivogel (Reitz, 219th, 17:04.0), Isaac Goedde (Reitz, 227th, 17:10.7), Chase Fuller (Reitz, 232nd, 17:17.8), Alton Kloppenstein (Barr-Reeve, 238th, 17:23.1), Landon Gaither (Barr-Reeve, 245th, 17:41.2) and Elliott Risch (Barr-Reeve, 250th, 18:47.4). IHSAA girls cross country championships Jasper finished in 23rd in team scoring in Terre Haute. Kylee Waninger of Heritage Hills finished in 59th place with a time of 18:43.1. Other individual results from Terre Haute: Ruth Dickason (Mater Dei, 99th, 19:08.5), Olivia Reckelhoff (Jasper, 113th, 19:15.3), Sophia Guth (Jasper, 143rd, 19:31.3), Kate Kelly (Jasper, 150th, 19:34.7), Rowen Englebright (North Posey, 185th, 19:53.7), Claire Buehler (Jasper, 232nd, 21:09.1), Ella Hopf (Jasper, 236th, 21:25.2), Molly Isaacs (Jasper, 243rd, 21:51.0), Allison Spaulding (Jasper, 249th, 22:44.6). Markos Tsegaye is a sports reporter for the Courier & Press. He can be reached at mtsegaye@usatodayco.com. Follow him on X @10_Markos_. This article originally appeared on Evansville Courier & Press: How SW Indiana teams, athletes fared at IHSAA cross country state finals

item.title: Woodridge cross country wins regional title by magnificent margin
item.description: BOARDMAN — "It's Woodridge." That's the answer to seemingly every impressive and even inexplicable thing the Bulldogs achieve in cross country. Fair enough, but the Woodridge boys securing the Division III boys team title by an 187-point margin shouldn't be taken for granted. The Bulldogs graduated two of the top four from last year's regional run in runner-up Atticus Sloan and Ben LeBay. Tack on Xavier Griffiths and they graduated three of last year's top 12. And they still scored just 37 points this year. Just like last year, Woodridge had two in the top four in runner-up John Brock (15:37.9), a senior, and fourth-place finisher Remington Griffiths (15:41.7), a junior. All told, the Bulldogs had four in the top nine, with junior Eli White (eighth, 16:13.0) and senior Nathan Adams (ninth, 16:15.4) running seconds apart, and six in the top 15. How? Well, it's Woodridge, but it shouldn't be taken for granted. Watch Ohio High School Sports Live on NFHS Network all year This story will be updated. item.title: Every player from Arkansas to play for the Golden State Warriors - Ron Brewer
item.description: The Golden State Warriors have signed, drafted, and traded for players from nearly every U.S. state and many countries around the world. From Alaska to Wyoming and Austria to Zaire, the Warriors have a strong history of seeking out talent necessary for NBA success. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor to the NBA) when they got their start as the team representing Philadelphia before they made their move to the West Coast, the organization has consistently pursued talent from a broad range of sources. For this installment of our series taking stock of the birthplace of every Golden State player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from Arkansas who has played for the Warriors. Our focus in this article is Ron Brewer. An alum of Northside high school and University of Arkansas-Fort Smith, Arkansas, he was picked up with the seventh overall selection of the 1978 NBA Draft by the Portland Trail Blazers. The Fort Smith, Arkansas native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career with Portland. He also played for the San Antonio Spurs , and Cleveland Cavaliers before he was dealt to the Golden State Warriors in 1982. His stay with the team lasted until he was traded to the San Antonio Spurs in 1984. During his time suiting up for the Warriors, Brewer put up 10.0 points, 1.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists, and 1.1 steals per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Warriors Wire: Every player from Arkansas to play for the Golden State Warriors - Ron Brewer

item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Josh Childress
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Josh Childress. An alum of Stanford, he was picked up with the sixth overall selection of the 2004 NBA Draft by the Atlanta Hawks. The Lakewood, California native played the first 4 seasons of his pro career with Atlanta. He also played in other leagues and for the Phoenix Suns before he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2012. His stay with the team lasted until he signed with the New Orleans Pelicans in 2013. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Childress put up 1.0 points and 1.1 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Nets Wire: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Josh Childress

item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 35 - Kenneth Faried (2019)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the 10th of 11 who wore the No. 35, Kenneth Faried. After ending his college career at Morehead State University, Faried was picked up with the 22nd overall selection of the 2011 NBA Draft by the Denver Nuggets. The Newark, New Jersey native played the first 7 seasons of his pro career with Denver, coming to an end when he was dealt to the Brooklyn Nets in 2018. That ended with his being cut in 2019, and signing with the Houston Rockets soon after for the final season of his NBA career. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Faried wore only jersey No. 35 and put up 12.9 points and 8.2 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. This article originally appeared on Rockets Wire: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 35 - Kenneth Faried (2019)

item.title: Sports media world absolutely baffled by Curt Cignetti’s timeout strategy
item.description: Credit: Rich Janzaruk/Herald-Times / USA TODAY NETWORK No. 4 Indiana escaped their matchup on Saturday against Minnesota with the win, but in true Halloween fashion, it came with quite a big scare. The game was tied 13–13 in the final minute of play with the Golden Gophers driving around midfield. After getting stopped on third down, Minnesota faced a decision to either go for it on fourth-and-8, attempt a kick at what would amount to a 60-yard field goal, or punt and hope to pin the Hoosiers and get to overtime. But while the biggest strategy question appeared to be in the hands of Minnesota coach P.J. Fleck, it was Indiana’s Curt Cignetti that wound up making a truly inexplicable decision. As the Gophers pondered what they would do, the clock ran and ran and ran, despite the fact that the Hoosiers had two timeouts. In basically every case, Indiana would want to use one of their timeouts in the spot, preserving time for their offense to secure a game-tying or game-winning field goal once possession changed hands. Instead, the clock ran all the way down to 24 seconds before Fleck took a timeout of his own and trotted out his field goal unit. At this point, people began to wonder what Cignetti was thinking. WHY in the world did Curt Cignetti not call a timeout to save his offense time after 3rd down??? Game management in college is AWFUL — Chase Daniel (@ChaseDaniel) October 31, 2026 Minnesota’s last offensive play of regulation was with 1:01 remaining. Curt Cignetti opted to not call a timeout. The Hoosiers finished regulation without using either timeout. https://t.co/IM8cDDqCCO — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) October 31, 2026 A rare Cignetti mistake. There was no detriment in calling timeout. It would’ve helped him if they made the field goal or missed it. It made no sense. — BucciOT.Com (@Buccigross) October 31, 2026 Why isn’t Indiana calling a timeout??? — Tim Murray (@1TimMurray) October 31, 2026 Minnesota kicker Luke Drzewiecki drilled it from 60 yards, and suddenly the upset was on, with the Gophers leading 16–13. Indiana had just 19 seconds (and two timeouts) to match the score, rather than having roughly a minute (and one timeout still!) had they called one earlier. HE NAILED IT FROM 60 YARDS!!!!!! GOPHERS LEAD LATE! “HAPPY HALLOWEEN LUKE DRZEWIECKI” — Brad Nessler https://t.co/KoDOSHPKei — CBS Sports College Football (@CBSSportsCFB) October 31, 2026 But the reigning champions still had fight in them. Quarterback Grant Wilson, who came in at halftime to replace Josh Hoover, connected with star receiver Charlie Becker to move the ball past midfield. While the clock stopped momentarily on the first down, it began to run once the ball was set. Again, in this spot, normally a timeout would be taken, especially if you have two of them. But Cignetti kept them in his pocket again. DIVING CATCH BY BECKER!! It made no sense. — BucciOT.Com (@Buccigross) October 31, 2026 Why isn’t Indiana calling a timeout??? — Tim Murray (@1TimMurray) October 31, 2026 Minnesota kicker Luke Drzewiecki drilled it from 60 yards, and suddenly the upset was on, with the Gophers leading 16–13. Indiana had just 19 seconds (and two timeouts) to match the score, rather than having roughly a minute (and one timeout still!) had they called one earlier. HE NAILED IT FROM 60 YARDS!!!!!! GOPHERS LEAD LATE! “HAPPY HALLOWEEN LUKE DRZEWIECKI” — Brad Nessler https://t.co/KoDOSHPKei — CBS Sports College Football (@CBSSportsCFB) October 31, 2026 But the reigning champions still had fight in them. Quarterback Grant Wilson, who came in at halftime to replace Josh Hoover, connected with star receiver Charlie Becker to move the ball past midfield. While the clock stopped momentarily on the first down, it began to run once the ball was set. Again, in this spot, normally a timeout would be taken, especially if you have two of them. But Cignetti kept them in his pocket again. DIVING CATCH BY BECKER!! CBS | Paramount+ https://t.co/vTkMwAB6lJ — CBS Sports College Football (@CBSSportsCFB) October 31, 2026 With two baffling timeout mistakes in less than 10 seconds of game time, the collective sports media world was having something of a breakdown wondering what the heck Cignetti was thinking. It is extremely hard to question the coaching decision of the man who took Indiana of all programs to an undefeated championship season last year, and yet, everyone at home seemed to understand the situation better than Cignetti in that moment. WHY DOES CURT CIGNETTI REFUSE TO CALL TIMEOUT?!?! https://t.co/XDmWJTopUO — College Sports Only (@CSOonX) October 31, 2026 All time bad clock management by Curt Cignetti — Football Analysis (@FBallAnalysisYT) October 31, 2026 So many strange game management decisions from Curt Cignetti but Indiana somehow got this to overtime. — Chris Vannini (@ChrisVannini) October 31, 2026 Cignetti is lucky they made that 60-yarder because not using either of his timeouts there was insanity — Max Chadwick (@CFBMaxChadwick) October 31, 2026 Cignetti not taking a timeout there is brutal. Did he think Becker was out of bounds? — Alex Barth (@RealAlexBarth) October 31, 2026 But it didn’t matter. Cignetti got bailed out after kicker Paddy McAteer drilled a 60-yarder of his own to tie the game and force overtime. HOWWWWWW?!?! ANOTHER 60 YARDER!!! PADDY MCATEER SENDS IT TO OVERTIME! CBS | Paramount+ https://t.co/P0NMHzQ7zb — CBS Sports College Football (@CBSSportsCFB) October 31, 2026 Luckily for Cignetti and Hoosiers fans across the country, there is no running clock in overtime, so the potential for timeout miscues was essentially zero for the rest of the night. Indiana scored a touchdown on their first play on offense, and was able to get the stop they needed on defense to seal the win. After the game went final, Cignetti seemed to at least partially acknowledge what an ugly sequence it took to even get to overtime. “It was really like, how many things you could do wrong and walk away with a really bad loss, even though Minnesota played great. And then finally with 19 seconds we woke up,” Cignetti told CBS reporter Jenny Dell. The Curt Cignetti postgame interview with CBS reporter Jenny Dell, capped off by Baby Ruth candy bars. https://t.co/cKrTL0zc3h — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 31, 2026 Speaking with reporters after the game , Cignetti explained his thinking behind both decisions. On the first, he said that had the kick been a little closer he might have stopped the clock, but he instead decided to let in run when he saw it was going to be 60 yards from the hash, which is about half of an answer. On the second, Cignetti said he thought the clock had been fully stopped because Becker got out of bounds, which checks out fully. With the dust now settled, Cignetti definitely got bailed out by his kicker. Had the Hoosiers not come back and won, his decisions not to call timeouts would be under far more scrutiny. Instead, the Hoosiers head into a bye week with a win and any questions can be answered with a vague, but genuine, “Yeah, we just needed every second to get out of there with a win.” The post Sports media world absolutely baffled by Curt Cignetti’s timeout strategy appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: UFC Vegas 123 live results, highlights, play-by-play
item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TONIGHT (Sat., Oct. 31, 2026) with UFC Halloween (a.k.a. UFC Vegas 123 ) , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event goes down inside the familiar META APEX in Las Vegas, Nevada. Our main event on this Halloween event is Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan ( see betting odds here ). UFC Halloween Preview It feels a little odd to see a UFC fight night land on Halloween. It would be nice if UFC did something to dress up for the occasion, but knowing them it will probably be business as usual. Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan draw the short straw of being unable to go trick or treating with their kids this night ( are you? ). They are meeting in the main event, despite Moicano saying he was desperate to escape the APEX. UFC Halloween’s co-main event is DC’s boy Jacobe Smith taking on the veteran Randy Brown ( on super short notice ). Smith has decimated all who have stood in his way so far. If he runs through Brown, then he’s a real player at 170 pounds . Rounding out UFC Halloween’s main card is Ode’ Osbourne vs. Cody Durden , Yana Santos vs. Luana Santos and Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani vs. Farman Hasanov . The “Prelims” are headlined by Francis Marshall vs. Dakota Hope . The biggest match-up on that portion of the card is Zachary Reese vs. Mickey Gall , with Gall looking to avoid his fifth straight loss. Former OKTAGON two-division champ Lucia Szabova also debuts at this event. She fights Tainara Lisboa . The rest of undercard includes Rodrigo Sezinando vs. Theodor Berggren , Julian Erosa vs. Jeong Yeong Lee ( in a retirement fight for Juicy J ), Nick Klein vs. Joseph Kropschott and Talita Alencar vs. Piera Rodriguez . UFC Halloween Start Date and Time We are back in the APEX tonight and that means a return to our usual broadcast times. UFC Halloween “Prelims” will begin at 5 p.m. ET . UFC Halloween main card is scheduled to start at 8 p.m. ET . All of Halloween airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here . The live blog here starts rolling below at 5 p.m. ET . Ode’ Osbourne via unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 135 lbs.: Luana Santos def. Yana Santos via unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) 170 lbs.: Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani vs. def. Tainara Lisboa via TKO (punches) — Round 3, 3:20 — HIGHLIGHTS UFC HALLOWEEN PLAY-BY-PLAY UPDATES Randy Brown vs. Jacobe Smith Round 1: Low kick from Smith misses to start the fight. Brown keeping distance, popping jabs and feinting knees. Smith spamming throwing leg kicks. Smith landed a right hand followed by a hard body kick. Smith finally landed a power double-leg takedown with 1:32 left in the round. Brown kept Smith tied up so not much damage was landed with the takedown. 10-9 Smith Ode Osbourne vs. Cody Durden Round 1: Low kick from Durden to start the fight. Durden got cracked by Osbourne and immediately shot for a takedown. Osbourne locked up a tight guillotine, but Durden eventually defended and got out. From there, he rode Osbourne and started dropping ground-and-pound. Durden took Osbourne’s back. After throwing some punches, Durden went for a face crank, but Osbourne defended. Durden tried to go for a Scottish Twister-type submission, and Osbourne defended. Durden started dropping heavy ground-and-pound, and seconds before the finish, Osbourne reversed him to end the round! 10-9 Durden Round 2: Durden shot immediately as the round started, but Osbourne defended. The two were tied up against the fence. The two got up, and Durden took him back down and controlled him for most of the round, dropping occasional ground-and-pound. Osbourne got back to his feet with 45 seconds left and touched Durden up with a couple of straight punches. 20-18 Durden Round 3: Body kick from Osbourne opened up the final round and soon after Durden shot for takedown. Osbourne initially defended but Durden got him down. Osbourne reversed! Durden got to the fence and was starting to get up before Osbourne jumped his back. Osbourne not really threatening anything just controlling Durden, and Durden is fine just riding out the clock. Durden eventually got out and dropped some punches to end the fight. 29-28 Durden 29-28 29-28 29-28 Cody Durden secures the W against Ode' Osbourne! 🤝 #UFCVegas123 | 🎥 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max ▶️ pic.twitter.com/h1vOUoVbu6 — UFC on TNT Sports (@ufcontnt) November 1, 2026 Official result: Durden def. Osbourne via unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) Yana Santos vs. Luana Santos Round 1: Luana tried for a trip/judo takedown to start the fight, but Yana defended and put Luana against the fence … for a good two minutes with no damage. Luana tried for the trip again, but Lana defended. At 1:12, the referee separated them. Yana cracked Luana with a right hand and then put her against the fence. Just a brutal round to watch. 10-9 Y. Santos Round 2: The two Santos’ started the second round striking before Luana landed a double-leg takedown and jumped to Yana’s back. Yana almost bucked Luana off before Luana forced her back down. With two minutes left, Luana landed really no damage, just control. Luana transitioned to mount but Yana just powered back to her feet. Luana took her right back down and ended in side control. 19-19 Round 3: Yana kept at range to prevent Luana from taking her down. Luana cracked her with a couple of overhands. Luana took her down and immediately took her back. Yana again almost bucked Luana off, but the Brazilian kept her control. Lana was punching Luana with Luana stuck on her back. item.title: France's Aymoz wins Skate Canada men's crown
item.description: French Olympian Kevin Aymoz won his second Figure Skating Grand Prix title at Skate Canada (WANG Zhao) French veteran Kevin Aymoz won the Skate Canada men's title on Saturday, capturing his second grand prix title as short program leader Rio Nakata faltered. Aymoz overcame miscues on his opening quadruple toe loop and triple Axel to deliver a characteristically suave free skate performance that garnered 168.17 points for a winning total of 258.43. Nakata, the two-time defending world junior champion, had led after the short program as he vied to capture gold on his senior grand prix debut. But the 18-year-old from Japan was fourth in the free skate, doubling two of his three planned quadruple jumps, to drop to second overall on 249.25 points Estonia's Mihhail Selevko was third on 248.66 after topping the final free skate. Aymoz, 29, claimed his second grand prix title, having ended a long wait for his first at Skate America last year -- eight years after making his grand prix level debut. He became the second-oldest man to win a grand prix title after Russian Sergei Veronov at 30 in 2017. Earlier Saturday another rising Japanese star, Mao Shimada, topped the women's short program with a score of 82.11. Shimada, who celebrated her 18th birthday on Friday, also made an impressive entry to the senior Grand Prix ranks. The four-time Junior Grand Prix Final and World Junior Championships winner, nailed a triple Axel as she finished in front of America's 2024 world silver medallist Isabeau Levito, who tallied 78.50. Estonia's Nina Petrokina was third on 71.95 heading into Sunday's free skate. Britain's Lila Fear and Lewis Gibson, the 2025 world bronze medallists, led the way after the ice dance rhythm dance ahead of France's Evgeniia Lopareva and Geoffrey Brissaud and Americans Caroline Green and Michael Parsons. bb/js

item.title: Purple Row After Dark: Which Rockies would survive a horror movie?
item.description: Nolan McDonald, 12, dressed as Jason Voorhees from "Friday the 13th," during Abington's 6th annual Oktoberfest at Island Grove Park on Saturday, Oct. 16, 2021. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Sometimes watching the Rockies can be particularly frightening. After 104 losses in 2026, Colorado fans have certainly endured their share of horror. But this Halloween, I’m flipping the script. Instead of asking how scary the Rockies can be, I’m asking which Rockies would actually survive a horror movie. If Jason Voorhees comes lumbering out of the woods with a machete in Friday the 13th , I’m taking Jake McCarthy. With his sprint speed, I like his chances of outrunning a masked killer. And as Sam put it, “Sorry, TJ!” Surviving Jigsaw’s traps in Saw requires patience, discipline and the ability to think through a difficult situation. I’m going with Kyle Karros and TJ Rumfield. Both have shown the ability to work an at-bat, recognize pitches and wait for something they can handle. While everyone else is panicking, these two are working the count. As for zombie movies, sometimes you don’t need speed or strategy. Sometimes you just need somebody who can hit something really hard. I’m taking Hunter Goodman and his 41 home runs. I’m not sure how barrel rate translates to fighting zombies, but I like his chances. Then there’s Scream , where Ghostface likes to call his victims before showing up at their homes. Unfortunately, Troy Johnston strikes me as the kind of guy who would answer the phone, politely engage in conversation and invite the killer inside. He’d probably offer him something to drink. I don’t like his chances of surviving the opening scene. And we can’t forget the ghost and ghoul films. Every good horror movie needs a ghost, and Coors Field already has one. I’m pretty sure Kris Bryant has been haunting the Rockies for years. Your turn, Purple Row. Which current Rockie would you trust to survive a horror movie? Who’s getting eliminated in the opening scene? There are thousands of great horror flicks out there, so feel free to share your favorites and tell me which Rockies you’d cast in them. Happy Halloween! Join the conversation! item.title: Patriots still has potential AJ Brown fantasy football replacements for Week 8
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Patriots still has potential AJ Brown fantasy football replacements for Week 8 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots are heading into Sunday’s AFC East matchup against the Miami Dolphins without two important offensive contributors. Wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) have both been ruled out , creating opportunities for other players to step up in Week 8. Brown’s absence leaves the Patriots with three healthy wide receivers on their 53-man roster: DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, and Kyle Williams. With Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins also unavailable, quarterback Drake Maye could rely more heavily on tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon to keep the passing attack productive. For fantasy football managers looking for alternatives, Douglas and Henry are two names worth monitoring. Douglas could see more opportunities working from the slot, while Henry may become a bigger part of the passing game as New England adjusts to its limited receiver depth. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Henderson’s absence also puts Rhamondre Stevenson in a favorable position to handle more offensive responsibilities. The veteran running back could receive additional carries while becoming a more frequent option in the passing game, making him another potential fantasy replacement to consider. The matchup against Miami could also work in New England’s favor. The Dolphins have struggled against opposing quarterbacks, ranking last in the NFL in pass EPA, passer rating allowed (116.8), and completion percentage allowed (76.6%). Despite the injuries, the Patriots still have several options capable of making an impact. Maye’s ability to distribute the ball could create opportunities for Douglas, Henry, and Stevenson to deliver useful fantasy production in Week 8. Related: Patriots’ AJ Brown, TreVeyon Henderson officially won’t play vs. Dolphins Related: Ranking top 3 Patriots most likely to be dealt at 2026 NFL trade deadline

item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell says Rick Bowness will tone it down
item.description: If Rick Bowness sounds more muted than usual after Blue Jackets losses, that's by design. More: Rick Bowness issues edict after Columbus Blue Jackets' ugly loss Speaking on a Blue Jackets Hockey Network broadcast during the first intermission Oct. 31 in Dallas, Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell said Bowness has been asked to save his most pointed criticisms for the locker room. That's mainly due to the veteran coach's epic postgame rant following the Blue Jackets' lackluster loss in a meaningless season finale last season. This season, he has publicly complained about the physical conditioning of two unnamed players to start training camp and then issued pointed comments after an ugly 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers on Oct. 13 at Nationwide Arena. After that game, Bowness said his players should feel "embarrassed" by their performance and shouldn't be part of the team if they didn't. Popular NHL podcasts and NHL TV broadcasts discussed the comments and some even suggested Bowness had "lost the locker room." Steve Mears, the Blue Jackets' play-by-play broadcaster, asked Waddell his thoughts about Bowness' pointed commentary during a conversation that included analyst Jody Shelley. "I think he's very emotional and he's very passionate for what he does," Waddell said. "I think he's done it a few times. I think we've talked about it. I don't know if we'll see that again." Bowness has held himself in check with his comments since the Jackets' blowout loss to the Panthers, including an assertion that his locker room's "culture" was no longer an issue after Kirill Marchenko and the Toronto Maple Leafs won 6-3 on Oct. 20 at Nationwide Arena. "What he says in the [locker room] will stay in the room," Waddell said. "But he's just so passionate for what he does and carries his emotions on his sleeve, and that's not a bad fault." Waddell was also asked if there was a player he'd like to take charge of the team's leadership while the team plays without a designated captain. "I had a great talk with [Mathieu Olivier on Oct. 30] about that whole concept," Waddell said. "He's a guy that's taken on more of a leadership role the few years. He's starting to play more and plays a huge factor for our team. He said it, 'We know we have to get it ... we met with the veteran leadership group. We talked about it. We need to be better.' He's got two goals, which is double some of the other guys, but I think he's taking a big part of that." Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Columbus Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell says Rick Bowness will tone it down

item.title: Liam Lawson disqualified from Mexico City Grand Prix qualifying
item.description: (Photo by Jayce Illman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Liam Lawson qualified eighth for Sunday’s Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix. But he will not line up in that spot on the grid ahead of the race. Lawson was cited for a failure to comply with the requirements of the F1 Regulations, specifically Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the sport’s technical regulations, which govern the energy deployment and power of the cars, and a required reduction of the MGU-K deployment. Here are the relevant sections of the F1 Technical Regulations : According to the report from the stewards, following qualifying a representative from Visa Cash App Racing Bulls, Lawson, the F1 single-seater Sporting Director, and members of the FIA Technical team including the FIA Technical Delegate, met with race officials. At the hearing, evidence was submitted showing that following the control line at the end of Lawson’s fastest lap in Q2, he did not lift off the power immediately. That resulted in the “rate of reduction of MGU-K deployment required to achieve the regulated ‘step down’ not being achieved.” VCARB argued that Lawson did not receive any performance advantage by not lifting off the throttle at the end of the lap, however, the Technical Regulations do not excuse non-compliance if no performance advantage is gained. In addition, the stewards noted that “these regulations require that a car must comply with them at all times during an event.” The stewards noted that while VCARB self-disclosed the breach, but precedents require the imposition of disqualification, even with mitigating factors present. You can read the full decision here: DOC 57 – Infringement – Car 30 – Technical nonconformity https://t.co/nVLPv627jK #MexicoGP #F1 #FIA pic.twitter.com/YrXGSVESxR — FIA (@fia) November 1, 2026 Lawson will now have to submit a request to the stewards to start the race, which will be granted under the sport’s “107% rule.” Under the F1 Sporting Regulations, since Lawson has set a satisfactory time within 107% of the fastest time during Q1 earlier in the week during practice, he will be permitted to start the race, from the back of the starting grid.

item.title: Texas football: Bloody hand doesn't stop Arch Manning on scoring drive vs Mississippi State
item.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates a touchdown by wide receiver Cam Coleman (8). During the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) After Texas football quarterback Arch Manning got bloody, the Longhorns got some points. Gianni Spetic 's 45-yard field goal gave Texas a 10-0 lead and capped a 13-play scoring drive for the Longhorns during the second quarter of Saturday's home game against Mississippi State . That drive featured a brief break while Manning tended to a cut on his right hand. Manning appeared to be bloodied at the end of a 10-yard scramble. Mississippi State's Bralan Womack was called for a personal foul at the end of that play. MORE: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter LIVE UPDATES: Follow along as Texas takes lead against Mississippi State Manning completed two passes after he had his hand taped. He also picked up another first down on a 6-yard run. That scoring drive also featured another play in which Manning lost his helmet after receiving a huge hit from Mississippi State edge rusher Amaree Williams. By rule, Manning had to leave the field for one play, and Texas had backup quarterback KJ Lacey hand off to Raleek Brown on that snap. item.title: 3 halftime observations from Ohio State vs. USC
item.description: Ohio State and USC have finished one half of football in the prime time Big Ten matchup in Los Angeles. The Buckeyes went into the locker room trailing 20-9 after a dominant first half for the Trojans . Both offenses have found success moving the ball down the field, but USC has converted on their opportunities while Ohio State has struggled to finish drives. Here are three things we took away from the first half in Los Angeles with Ohio State and USC. Trent Mosley is a big problem for the Buckeyes The USC freshman wide receiver has been putting on a show for the Trojans. On the second play from scrimmage, Jayden Maiava dumped off a screen pass to Mosley who turned up the field for 69 yards and the score. Trent Mosley breaks free for a MASSIVE USC touchdown! 😤 📺 Ohio State at USC on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/ZGdRhgQ1LA — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) October 31, 2026 Mosley continued to make a big impact in the first half as he recorded four more receptions bringing his total yardage to 101 yards. He also proved his value on special teams, returning a punt 44 yards setting up USC’s second touchdown of the game. Ohio State will need to eliminate Mosley in the second half to slow down the Trojan offense. Ohio State needs to convert in the red zone The Buckeyes found success moving the ball in the first half but have failed to find the end zone. Ohio State amounted 192 total offensive yards and have visited the red zone on two separate occasions. Both times the Buckeyes had to settle for field goals. On the first Ohio State offensive drive, the Buckeyes stalled out on the USC 21-yard line. The promising opening drive ended in three points which seemed like a win after Luke Fahey’s pass was nearly intercepted on third down. After falling down 14-3, it seemed like the Ohio State offense was going to respond, but a costly illegal substitution penalty caused a third and long for the Buckeyes. Ultimately, Ohio State was forced to kick another field goal. The most heartbreaking drive for the Buckeyes came near the end of the half. Ohio State thought it scored their first touchdown on a Luke Fahey tush push play, but after review, the ball was ruled just short of the goal line. The Trojan defense then held strong, and the Buckeyes called on Connor Hawkins for the third time in the game. Ohio State must convert on their opportunities in the second half if it wants to find a way to win this game against USC. Jeremiah Smith is still unstoppable There were a lot of question marks heading into this game surrounding the Ohio State offense. With the injury to quarterback Julian Sayin , the true freshman Luke Fahey has taken the reigns under center. item.content:encoded: Ohio State and USC have finished one half of football in the prime time Big Ten matchup in Los Angeles. The Buckeyes went into the locker room trailing 20-9 after a dominant first half for the Trojans . Both offenses have found success moving the ball down the field, but USC has converted on their opportunities while Ohio State has struggled to finish drives. Here are three things we took away from the first half in Los Angeles with Ohio State and USC. Trent Mosley is a big problem for the Buckeyes The USC freshman wide receiver has been putting on a show for the Trojans. On the second play from scrimmage, Jayden Maiava dumped off a screen pass to Mosley who turned up the field for 69 yards and the score. Trent Mosley breaks free for a MASSIVE USC touchdown! 😤 📺 Ohio State at USC on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/ZGdRhgQ1LA — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) October 31, 2026 Mosley continued to make a big impact in the first half as he recorded four more receptions bringing his total yardage to 101 yards. He also proved his value on special teams, returning a punt 44 yards setting up USC’s second touchdown of the game. Ohio State will need to eliminate Mosley in the second half to slow down the Trojan offense. Ohio State needs to convert in the red zone The Buckeyes found success moving the ball in the first half but have failed to find the end zone. Ohio State amounted 192 total offensive yards and have visited the red zone on two separate occasions. Both times the Buckeyes had to settle for field goals. On the first Ohio State offensive drive, the Buckeyes stalled out on the USC 21-yard line. The promising opening drive ended in three points which seemed like a win after Luke Fahey’s pass was nearly intercepted on third down. After falling down 14-3, it seemed like the Ohio State offense was going to respond, but a costly illegal substitution penalty caused a third and long for the Buckeyes. Ultimately, Ohio State was forced to kick another field goal. The most heartbreaking drive for the Buckeyes came near the end of the half. Ohio State thought it scored their first touchdown on a Luke Fahey tush push play, but after review, the ball was ruled just short of the goal line. The Trojan defense then held strong, and the Buckeyes called on Connor Hawkins for the third time in the game. Ohio State must convert on their opportunities in the second half if it wants to find a way to win this game against USC. Jeremiah Smith is still unstoppable There were a lot of question marks heading into this game surrounding the Ohio State offense. With the injury to quarterback Julian Sayin , the true freshman Luke Fahey has taken the reigns under center. It was hard to know how this change would affect the Heisman favorite , but so far, it seems that Jeremiah Smith will continue to dominate. The Buckeyes made it obvious on their first offensive drive that they will continue to rely on their leading receiver. Fahey found Smith on Ohio State’s first offensive play and looked his way most of the half. The freshman quarterback completed only eight passes with five of them going to Smith. In the first half, Smith recorded 35 yards on the five receptions. The star wide receiver demonstrated his talent creating separation and making contested catches. Ohio State must continue to call his number if it wants to come back in this one. This article originally appeared on Buckeyes Wire: 3 halftime observations from Ohio State vs. USC

item.title: Maple Leafs Defeat Canucks In Competitive Halloween Showdown
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was a Halloween night affair at Rogers Arena as the Toronto Maple Leafs came to town against the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday night. The Leafs, on the heels of an impressive second period, were able to win the game, 4-2. Toronto, with the win, now has an 8-6-2 record, while Vancouver drops to 3-12-1. Here is the recap for the Maple Leafs vs Canucks game. Game Stories: Meriläinen’s Fourth Consecutive Start, Quillan’s Season Debut The Canucks gave goaltender Leevi Meriläinen a fourth consecutive start, which is telling about how the team feels about their goaltending. Meriläinen has had his numbers regress back to his career averages after he posted a save percentage above .900 in his first six appearances, but he has given his team a chance every night. Jacob Quillan was called up to Vancouver after Filip Chytil was placed on injured reserve on Friday and made his season debut tonight against his former team. He was a key piece in the Aatu Räty trade on October 15. Quillan slotted in on the third line alongside Liam Öhgren and Linus Karlsson . A Relatively Even First Period The Canucks were spooked to start this game, as Jamie Oleksiak had a blunder at the Toronto blue line, which resulted in a breakaway for William Nylander , giving the Leafs an early lead at 1:21. Breakaway Willy, haunting goalies 😈 pic.twitter.com/Olx1VEwmDM — Toronto Maple Leafs (@MapleLeafs) October 31, 2026 After failing to score on their first power play, the Canucks got a breakaway of their own on their second man advantage, as Filip Hronek threw a long pass up the ice to Brock Boeser instead of making the drop pass. It paid off as Boeser was able to capitalize on the breakaway to tie the game. One thing the Canucks need to do more on the power play is make more unpredictable plays, which Hronek did a good job of on the second one. Notably, Elias Pettersson drew both the Toronto penalties in the first period. BROCK BOESER TIES IT ‼️ pic.twitter.com/9E2SFVDxdN — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 31, 2026 Penalties kept coming fast and furious, as the Canucks found themselves shorthanded on a 5-on-3 situation, with penalties to Drew O’Connor and Jamie Oleksiak. With some help from the post, the Canucks were able to kill it off, with tenacious blocking and getting into shot lanes. 1-1 after 20 minutes, with the Canucks outshooting the Leafs 13-9. A good start, sans the early blunder. Leafs Pounce on Bad Canuck Bounces in Second Period The Leafs started the second with another early goal, with Auston Matthews putting one home from a sharp angle at 3:47 to make it 2-1. Elias Pettersson’s stick shattered after blocking a shot from Darren Raddysh , giving the Leafs a bit of extra room. Meriläinen would likely want that goal back. That was BOO-tiful 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/8o9nISAabD — Toronto Maple Leafs (@MapleLeafs) November 1, 2026 Toronto would keep pressing and have most of the pressure in the second period, and on an extended shift in the Canuc

item.title: Comparing UC Bearcats loss to No. 6 Utah to previous wipeouts
item.description: Before the Halloween haymakers were thrown at Nippert Stadium, the Cincinnati Bearcats had the No. 8 rushing offense in the NCAA at 234.6 yards per game, compared to the Utes No. 8 rushing defense. But the key was Utah's 10th-ranked red zone defense, which kept UC out of the end zone in the first half, with the Utes taking the Bearcats to the proverbial woodshed, 42-6. It evoked bad memories of a night in Tampa when Tommy Tuberville's 2015 Bearcats were down 51-3 to USF at the break. The 42 points were just three away from what the Utes scored last year in Salt Lake City, dismantling the Bearcats 45-14. Alas, UC would outscore Utah 19-7 in the second half Oct. 31 to make for the more presentable score of 49-25. However, many of the 36,487 at Nippert were off to various "Monster Mashes," down 35 at halftime. "It was a lot to a little", UC head coach Scott Satterfield said. "I don't blame them for leaving when the score's like that at halftime. I'm proud of our guys for the way they came back and fought in the second half. The game was out of hand there at halftime, but our guys keep playing." Difficult halftime deficits for Cincinnati Bearcats As mentioned, the 51-3 deficit at USF in 2015 turned into a 65-27 loss. Before the halftime hammering by No. 6 Utah, UC's worst deficit this season after two quarters was to Miami University 28-7 at TQL Stadium. The Bearcats came back to win that one 35-31. The closest UC got against the Utes was 24 when JC French added a 2-yard score early in the fourth quarter. As rough as the defense was, UC did stop a Utes 4th-and-goal attempt from the 1-yard line with 1:17 to go to keep them from going over 50 points. The last team to score 50 points on the Bearcats was Ohio State, which beat a Tuberville team in 2014, 50-28. The last team to reach 49 vs. UC and Satterfield was Kansas, which spoiled Senior Night in 2023 with a 49-16 shellacking of the 'Cats. The 33-point defeat is their worst in Big 12 play. Other dastardly defeats in UC Bearcats history In Satterfield's opening year of 2023, the Bearcats were pounded in Stillwater by Oklahoma State, 45-13, a 32-point loss . Last year's Utes loss was by 31 points, and this year's loss at Arizona was by 27, 34-7. In 2024, they lost at Kansas State by 26, 41-15. In 2025, UC lost by 22 at TCU, 45-23 (and also in the Jan. 1 FedEx Bowl to Navy, 35-13). In 2023, the Bearcats fell in Morgantown to West Virginia by 21, 42-21. More UC teams blown out in recent years Before Luke Fickell led the Bearcats to the College Football Playoff in 2021, he suffered his own blowouts. In 2019, the Bearcats were blanked in Columbus by Ohio State 42-0, Worse yet, his 2017 team lost to UCF at Nippert 51-23, in a game called after three quarters due to thunderstorms. The all-time whipping remains 1991's 81-0 drubbing at No. 5 Penn State, with Joe Paterno's Nittany Lions taking it to an inferior Bearcats team. UC wasn't alone in winning big, then losing big The same weekend UC lost to No. 6 Utah

If somebody could figure this out and you could get your guys to go out and play every week, it'd be awesome. Right now, there's only two or three teams that are undefeated. Each game is a new season for every team." UC's new season is Sunday, Nov. 7 at Houston, which didn't play this weekend. item.title: Liam Lawson disqualified from F1 qualifying in Mexico – here's why
item.description: Motorsport photo Liam Lawson has lost his ninth-place starting position for the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix. Racing Bulls impressed at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Saturday and managed to get both cars into Q3. The team subsequently emerged as the 'best of the rest' in eighth and ninth places, but Lawson now faces a recovery drive on Sunday. The New Zealander has been disqualified by the FIA for a technical infringement. The summons document had already stated that “Lawson was in breach of the minimum MGU-K power requirement just after crossing the line on his fastest lap in Q2 at 15:47:36.” Following a visit to the stewards, the outcome was the same as for almost all technical infringements: disqualification. In practice, Lawson did not immediately lift off the throttle after completing his fastest Q2 lap, meaning he failed to comply with the prescribed MGU-K rampdown rate. That electrical power must be reduced gradually in accordance with Article C5.12.6 of the technical regulations. It stipulates maximum reductions of either 50 or 100kW per second: “The driver maximum power demand must not be reduced at any greater than the rates defined below whilst the electrical DC power of the ERS-K is above 100kW: a. 50kW in any 1s period at Competitions where the FIA determines that the power limited distance exceeds 3500m. The vehicle fundamentals used for the calculation of the power limited distance may be found in the document FIA-F1-DOC-034. b. 100kW in any 1s period at all other Competitions.” In Lawson's case, that rampdown rate of the electrical power was steeper after he failed to lift off the throttle immediately upon crossing the line, as described in the stewards' report. “Evidence submitted, which was accepted by all parties present, showed that after the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, the driver did not lift off the power immediately. This resulted in the rate of reduction of MGU-K deployment required to achieve the regulated “step down”, not being achieved.” The summons document further clarified this breach as follows: “The driver maximum power demand and the electrical DC power of the ERS-K were reduced at greater rates than what is permitted by the Regulations.” Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls During the hearing, all parties concluded that Racing Bulls had gained no sporting advantage from the infringement, although that finding was not enough to prevent the disqualification. Technical infringements are, after all, always black and white. “The team argued that this did not provide any performance advantage however it is clear that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused if no performance advantage is gained. Further, these regulations require that a car must comply with them at all times during an event. “The Stewards note in particular that the team self-disclosed the breach however there are a multitude of precedents that require us, despite all mitigating circums
item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Liam Lawson has lost his ninth-place starting position for the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix. Racing Bulls impressed at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Saturday and managed to get both cars into Q3. The team subsequently emerged as the 'best of the rest' in eighth and ninth places, but Lawson now faces a recovery drive on Sunday. The New Zealander has been disqualified by the FIA for a technical infringement. The summons document had already stated that “Lawson was in breach of the minimum MGU-K power requirement just after crossing the line on his fastest lap in Q2 at 15:47:36.” Following a visit to the stewards, the outcome was the same as for almost all technical infringements: disqualification. In practice, Lawson did not immediately lift off the throttle after completing his fastest Q2 lap, meaning he failed to comply with the prescribed MGU-K rampdown rate. That electrical power must be reduced gradually in accordance with Article C5.12.6 of the technical regulations. It stipulates maximum reductions of either 50 or 100kW per second: “The driver maximum power demand must not be reduced at any greater than the rates defined below whilst the electrical DC power of the ERS-K is above 100kW: a. 50kW in any 1s period at Competitions where the FIA determines that the power limited distance exceeds 3500m. The vehicle fundamentals used for the calculation of the power limited distance may be found in the document FIA-F1-DOC-034. b. 100kW in any 1s period at all other Competitions.” In Lawson's case, that rampdown rate of the electrical power was steeper after he failed to lift off the throttle immediately upon crossing the line, as described in the stewards' report. “Evidence submitted, which was accepted by all parties present, showed that after the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, the driver did not lift off the power immediately. This resulted in the rate of reduction of MGU-K deployment required to achieve the regulated “step down”, not being achieved.” The summons document further clarified this breach as follows: “The driver maximum power demand and the electrical DC power of the ERS-K were reduced at greater rates than what is permitted by the Regulations.” Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls During the hearing, all parties concluded that Racing Bulls had gained no sporting advantage from the infringement, although that finding was not enough to prevent the disqualification. Technical infringements are, after all, always black and white. “The team argued that this did not provide any performance advantage however it is clear that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused if no performance advantage is gained. Further, these regulations require that a car must comply with them at all times during an event. “The Stewards note in particular that the team self-disclosed the breach however there are a multitude of precedents that require us, despite all mitigating circumstances, to impose a penalty of Disqualfication where a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations.” It means Lawson will have to start from the very back of the grid on Sunday and faces a fight through the field. The disqualification is good news for Alpine , with one of its rivals for fifth place in the constructors' championship now forced to start from the back. In the standings, however, Racing Bulls still holds a comfortable 33-point advantage.
